initial_requirements: Users need a video-search application that can query multiple websites at once for streaming sources and downloadable video listings. A user should be able to search for a specific title or genre, choose which types of sources to include, compare organized results, and retain useful favorites. System maintainers also need a way to control which external sites participate in searches.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the core functions the video-search application must provide from the user’s perspective, including searching, filtering source types, comparing results, and saving or managing favorites?
turns.interviewee_utterance: From the user’s side, the app needs to let them search for a title or browse by genre, then pull back results from multiple sites in one place. They should be able to filter what kind of sources they want to see, like streaming-only or downloadable listings, and compare the results in a clean, organized view. It also needs a way for users to save favorites and manage that list later, so they can come back to useful sources without searching again.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Who are the key stakeholder groups involved in this application—such as end users, system maintainers, site administrators, or others—and what responsibilities or needs does each group have?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The main groups are the end users and the system maintainers. End users need fast searching across multiple sites, filtering by source type, and a way to save favorites, while maintainers need control over which external sites are included in searches and probably some visibility into whether those sources are working well. If there are site administrators or content partners involved, I’d need to verify that, because that hasn’t been defined yet.

turns.interviewer_utterance: For the external sources included in search, what source health monitoring should the system provide to maintainers—for example, which availability or performance indicators should be tracked, how often should they be checked, and what alerts or dashboard visibility would be most useful?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Maintainers would definitely need to know when a source stops responding, starts timing out, or returns broken or empty results, because that directly affects search quality. I’d also want some basic performance indicators like response time and maybe last successful crawl or check, but I’m not sure yet how detailed that needs to be. A dashboard showing each source’s current status, last check time, and any recent failures would be useful, and alerts should probably fire when a source is down for more than a short period or failing repeatedly.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When a source becomes unreliable or fails repeatedly, how should the system decide whether to deprioritize it in search results, temporarily exclude it from searches, or keep it visible but flagged to maintainers?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I’d expect the system to use a simple threshold approach at first, where repeated failures or consistently poor response times move the source into a warning state and then a disabled state if it keeps happening. If it’s only flaky, it could still appear in results but be ranked lower or flagged for maintainers; if it’s clearly down, it should be temporarily excluded from searches until it recovers. The exact thresholds would need to be agreed with the team, because I don’t know yet how aggressive we want to be.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Provide a video-search app that aggregates streaming and downloadable video listings from multiple websites, allowing users to search by title or genre, filter source types, compare organized results, and save/manage favorites.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Primary stakeholder groups are end users and system maintainers. End users need fast multi-site searching, source-type filtering, and favorites management. System maintainers need control over which external sites are included in searches and visibility into source health and reliability. Other stakeholder groups such as site administrators or content partners are not yet confirmed.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Search by title or genre, query multiple websites at once, filter results by source type (e.g., streaming-only or downloadable listings), present results in a clean organized/comparable view, and allow users to save and manage favorites.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: A simple threshold-based approach should govern source reliability handling: repeated failures or consistently poor response times move a source into a warning state and then a disabled state if issues continue; flaky sources may remain visible but ranked lower or flagged for maintainers; clearly down sources should be temporarily excluded from searches until they recover. Exact thresholds are not yet defined.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: Source reliability and search quality are important; maintainers need visibility into source responsiveness, timing, broken/empty results, response time, last successful crawl/check, current status, last check time, and recent failures.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: When a source stops responding, times out, or returns broken/empty results, it should be treated as a failure. If failures are repeated or the source is down for more than a short period, alert maintainers and temporarily exclude the source from searches until it recovers.

slots.name: source_administration
slots.value: System maintainers need the ability to control which external sites are included in searches and may need visibility into whether those sources are functioning well.

slots.name: source_health_monitoring
slots.value: Monitor when a source stops responding, times out, returns broken or empty results, and track current status, last check time, recent failures, response time, and last successful crawl/check; alert when a source is down for more than a short period or failing repeatedly.

slots.name: source_reliability_metrics
slots.value: Track response time, last successful crawl/check, current status, last check time, and recent failures as indicators of source reliability.

slots.name: source_failure_handling
slots.value: Treat stopped responses, timeouts, broken results, and empty results as source failures; surface them in the dashboard and trigger alerts when failures persist or repeat.

slots.name: source_priority_rules
slots.value: Sources with repeated failures or consistently poor response times should move from normal to warning and then disabled states. Flaky sources may still appear in results but be ranked lower and flagged; clearly down sources should be excluded from searches until recovery.

slots.name: source_deprioritization_rules
slots.value: If a source is only flaky, it can remain visible but should be ranked lower or flagged for maintainers. Repeated failures or poor response times should cause warning then disabled status, with exact thresholds to be agreed later.

slots.name: source_status_dashboard
slots.value: A dashboard should show each source’s current status, last check time, recent failures, and likely response-time/reliability indicators, so maintainers can quickly see which sources are healthy or problematic.

abduction_history.suspected_reason: Because the application depends on third-party websites, source availability, latency, and result quality are likely operational risks. The business may need monitoring and source health insight to keep search results trustworthy and to quickly disable or deprioritize unreliable sites.
